subject: Bancorp - eval plan & next steps
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@bancorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Hwang <tom.hwang@bancorp.com>
Date: Sat, 9 May 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up + eval scope (Bancorp)

Thanks again for the call today \u0014 quick recap and a few asks so we can move the eval forward.

Recap:
- Use case: customer support triage + first-pass intent classification for regulated banking transcripts (chat + short email).
- Constraints: PII redaction required, higher precision on fraud/AML flags, latency target ~300ms P50 for short prompts, budget-sensitive.

Requested next steps:
1) Recommended model(s) and baseline we should test on Redwood (we need smaller footprints for on-prem vs hosted comparison).
2) Eval checklist: dataset format, scoring rubric, and how you handle sampling & random seeds.
3) Logistics: how to securely upload sample prompts, and an estimate for how long a 10k prompt eval will take.

I'll attach a 200-row sample prompt set to start (bancorp_sample_prompts.csv).

Appreciate it \u0014 happy to set a follow-up call if helpful.

\u0014Elena
VP Ops, Bancorp Financial

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@bancorp.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up + eval scope (Bancorp)

Hi Elena \u0014 great talking yesterday. Thanks for the clear list, that helps a lot. Below is a proposed plan and answers to each of your asks.

1) Model recommendations (short-term vs. POC):
- Hosted quick baseline: small/medium open models we recommend to start: Mistral-Inference-7B, Llama2-13B-8bit (quantized). These balance accuracy vs. latency for short classification tasks.
- Private/Dedicated POC: Redwood-Prod-v1 (13B quantized + KV cache optimizations) and a 30B variant if you want to stress quality tradeoffs.
- If strict latency/budget constraints, we can test a distilled 3B candidate for comparison.

2) Eval checklist / scoring rubric (summary):
- Dataset format: CSV with columns: id, prompt, reference, metadata_json. We'll include a template (bancorp_eval_template.csv).
- Scoring: we recommend a 0-3 ordinal rubric for classification tasks (0=incorrect, 1=partial, 2=mostly correct, 3=exact). For binary fraud flags we use precision/recall and F1 at the threshold you care about.
- Sampling & seeds: we'll run 3 randomized shuffles (seeded) and report mean + stdev for aggregate metrics.
- Privacy: PII redaction recommended pre-upload; we can run on-prem or in your VPC if you prefer.

3) Logistics & timing:
- Secure upload options: S3 presigned, direct upload to your private Red region, or SFTP. For PCI/PHI customers we recommend the VPC upload flow (link below).
- Run time: a 10k prompt eval on a dedicated 13B instance typically completes in ~2-6 hours depending on batch size and model. We will provide a concrete estimate after seeing average prompt length.

4) Deliverables and next steps:
- Redwood will provide: detailed eval report (accuracy, per-class confusion, latency percentiles, token cost), model recommendations, and prompt set suggestions.
- Ask: can you confirm whether you want us to run on hosted Redwood or set up a Private eval in your VPC? If private, we'll loop in our infra team to scope network access.

Attachments: bancorp_eval_template.csv, redwood_eval_checklist.pdf. Benchmark links: https://redwood-internal.company/docs/eval-guides/baseline-benchmarks

If helpful, I'm free for a quick 30-min sync Tue/Wed to walk through the template and the data ingestion.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales Rep | Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Elena Morales <elena.morales@bancorp.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 08:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up + eval scope (Bancorp)

Thanks \u0014 adding a few technical details on the eval harness and dataset format to avoid back-and-forth: 

- File format: UTF-8 CSV, newline-delimited. Required columns:
  * id (unique string)
  * prompt (string)
  * reference (string; expected classification label or gold response)
  * metadata_json (single-quoted JSON blob for metadata like channel, timestamp, language)

- Prompt pre-processing:
  * Keep prompts under 1024 tokens for the initial run; if you have longer transcripts we'll provide a segmenter.
  * Strip direct PII if possible; if not, we can apply a redaction pass (we'll need approval and an SLA for redaction rules).

- Scoring & aggregation:
  * For intent classification: label-level accuracy, macro/micro F1, and confusion matrix export.
  * For open-ended responses (if any): we'll run both automated metrics (ROUGE/BLEU where applicable) and a small human eval sample (n=200) for quality checks.

- Reproducibility:
  * We run each model configuration 3x with seeds [42, 101, 2026] and provide aggregated mean & standard deviation.

- Security: uploads can be scoped to a pre-signed S3 OR sent to our private ingestion endpoint in your VPC. We'll generate a one-time upload token.

I'll stand by to help with the template mapping \u0014 if you share a sample CSV (the 200-row file Marissa mentioned) I can validate it and run a quick smoke eval on a single instance to sanity-check formatting.

\u0014Dev
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@bancorp.com>

Thanks Marissa/Dev \u0014 this is super helpful. A few clarifications: 

- We'll start with hosted runs (faster) to get baseline numbers, then move to Private for the final POC.
- Confirmed: we'll remove direct account numbers and social IDs from the sample and keep PII redaction for later.
- Timeline: aim to have a validated sample by EOD Tuesday (2026-05-12). If that works, can you run a smoke eval Wed morning and share preliminary metrics by Wed EOD?

Attached: bancorp_sample_prompts.csv (200 rows). Please run the format validator and let me know any issues.

\u0014Elena

Marissa
